thread:
maria.g: Heads-up — the int4 onboard for rwd-v2.7 saw a 2.8% concordance drop on long-doc slice in the first canary. Traffic was 1% for 30m. Can we triage thresholds?

jamal: Seen the alert. Link to the run: https://ci.redwood/internal/runs/7865

sophia: Quick context — int4 means nf4 quant; baseline is v2.6 float16. What metrics failed? 

maria.g: concordance delta = -2.8% (90% CI), hallucination_rate +0.3pp, latency_p95 +40ms. p50 unchanged. sample size ~3k queries.

dmitri: That concordance delta is above our soft threshold (1.5%) but below auto-rollback (5%). We should not fall back automatically yet. 

sophia: Agreed. We should tighten the canary dispatcher thresholds: auto-fallback if concordance_delta <= -5% OR hallucination_rate increase >= 1.0pp OR latency_p95 > 600ms. Soft alert at -1.5%/+0.25pp. 

maria.g: Proposal: add cooldown/hysteresis so we need two consecutive windows (15m each) exceeding a threshold before triggering rollback. Also add slice-specific gates for long-docs. 

jamal: +1 for hysteresis. Also, can we make fallback degrade traffic to 0.1% then to 0% instead of full immediate failover? That reduces oscillation. 

dmitri: We already support progressive drain in dispatcher; change required is policy values. Suggested ramp: 1% -> 0.1% (10m) -> 0% if persists another 10m. 

sophia: Add a forced manual lock for on-call if the concordance delta is between -5% and -10% but hallucination spike small — sometimes quality metrics are noisy. 

canary-bot: deploy-notify: canary rwd-v2.7-int4 started at 1709998200, current traffic 0.5%, steady-state 30m.

maria.g: Action items: (1) jamal update dispatcher policy with hysteresis and progressive drain; (2) dmitri add slice-aware gate for long-docs and tighten soft alert thresholds; (3) sophia draft runbook update for manual lock and quick rollback steps. I'll follow up with a quick smoke eval after policy change. 

jamal: I'll push policy change in 20m and shadow-run with no rollout for 1 hour. 

sophia: I'll prep a small eval suite focusing on long-context and codeblocks. 

dmitri: FYI — we should also log per-token prefix KV hit rates to rule out cache warmup as cause. 

maria.g: Good call. If we still see concordance drift after cache stabilized, escalate to model-onboarding. 

jamal: ack. 

sophia: :thumbsup:

maria.g: thanks everyone — keeping this thread for the policy diffs and later post-mortem.
